courses.name: Theoretical Machine Learning
courses.description: Examines approximation, optimization and generalization in classical learning and deep neural networks.

courses.name: Data Mining
courses.description: Covers data preparation, pattern discovery, classification, clustering and advanced data-mining applications.

courses.name: Deep Learning
courses.description: Connects deep-learning theory with practical image and language applications.

courses.name: Machine Learning
courses.description: Studies mathematical foundations and algorithms for classification, regression and decision making through programming projects.

courses.name: Natural Language Processing
courses.description: Surveys statistical and neural language processing, foundation models and language-understanding applications.

courses.name: Machine Vision
courses.description: Introduces image formation and processing, object recognition and geometric and statistical vision models.

courses.name: End-to-End Deep Learning
courses.description: Studies deployment, data management, fairness, monitoring and operational management of deep-learning systems.

courses.name: Machine Learning Systems for Efficient AI
courses.description: Studies programming, compilation, parallelization and hardware for efficient large-scale AI systems.

requirements.title: Five advanced courses for the concentration
requirements.summary: Five distinct four-credit advanced CS courses numbered 200 or higher; one more course than the base BS requires.

requirements.title: At least three AI-area courses
requirements.summary: At least three of the five courses must be in the approved AI area. Additional unused AI-area courses may fill the remaining two positions.

requirements.title: Two remaining advanced-course positions
requirements.summary: Two additional eligible four-credit advanced CS courses numbered 200 or higher, including unused AI-area choices. This is an open course-number rule, not a missing finite approved list.

requirements.title: Core and math exclusions
requirements.summary: Advanced-course choices exclude the parent program core and additional math courses listed on the same source page.

requirements.title: Optional concentration within CS BS
requirements.summary: This is an optional concentration for BS Computer Science students; it does not constitute a standalone AI degree.

requirements.title: Limit on outside core/major electives
requirements.summary: No more than two core or major electives may be completed at other institutions, except through the University's education-abroad program.

requirements.title: Approval of transfer coursework
requirements.summary: Transfer courses used for CS major requirements require approval from the corresponding department; submit course approval materials and syllabi for CS evaluation.

requirements.title: Changes to the CS course plan
requirements.summary: Discuss changes to the official CS course plan with the CS undergraduate coordinator.

notes: Complete designation covers the local concentration inventory, not the full CS BS. At least three of five courses must be approved AI courses; the other two may include unused AI courses or other eligible advanced CS courses.
The general advanced-course rule is open: course number 200 or higher, four credits, excluding core/additional math courses listed by the parent degree. It is not an unavailable finite elective list.

Five courses, each four credits, is a requirement constraint. Individual catalog credits were not independently verified, so each course record keeps credits null rather than asserting catalog metadata.

Transfer limit is two outside core/major electives, with the published education-abroad exception; departmental approval remains necessary. Changes to the official course plan go through the CS undergraduate coordinator.

Eight descriptions are now reviewed. Formal prerequisites, unit/calendar normalization, catalog edition, launch date and public course resources remain unverified. Primary source was read from permitted cache fetched 2026-10-10T21:59:27+00:00; advising source was fetched in this review.

CSC 244 and CSC 266 are not represented in these two schedules; this is not evidence of discontinuation or exclusion.
